tasks.short: Sponsor clubs, student organisations and contests

steps.what: Sponsor extracurricular activities through guidance, participation and appropriate supervision

tasks.design: Keep extracurricular sponsorship and supervision with the teacher. Existing school activity guidance in {DOCS} supports the role; no separate event-administration baseline or automated sponsor is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Students need an adult who understands the activity and can guide responsible participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing guidance already supports the human sponsorship role.
tasks.still_hard: A club can need encouragement, conflict resolution or a safety decision during activity.
tasks.human_edge: Support student initiative while recognising when intervention is necessary.
tasks.altitude: Sponsorship responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Extracurricular sponsorship and live guidance retain their labour without an assumed paperwork saving.

assumptions: Boundary is teacher sponsorship and supervision, excluding student organisation work and separately assigned bookings or procurement.
No new structured club-performance input or automated decision is introduced.
Existing native policy access suffices. No deployment or additional maintenance is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which situations need teacher intervention rather than student-led resolution?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Sponsorship and supervision remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on school programme development and revision

steps.what: Review programme evidence and prepare a professional contribution
Collaborate with teachers and administrators on programme evaluation and revision

tasks.design: Keep professional evidence review and programme deliberation with the teacher and colleagues using {DOCS}. Drafting a separate programme document is not assumed within this collaboration task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme choices require reconciling educational, occupational and resource priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing programme evidence already supports the retained discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Different departments may value different outcomes and face different constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Bring practical teaching evidence into a collective decision and engage with disagreement.
tasks.altitude: Programme collaboration time and decision rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Programme evidence interpretation and collaboration retain their labour; no new document-production baseline is invented.

assumptions: Boundary is the teacher's preparation and collaborative discussion, excluding independent curriculum writing and administrators' work.
No new structured programme score or automated decision is required.
Existing native document access suffices. No deployment or additional upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Programme review remit and available evidence
research_questions: Which proposed changes are supported by classroom and workplace evidence?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Professional interpretation and collaboration remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend professional meetings, conferences and workshops

steps.what: Attend professional meetings, conferences and workshops to improve competence

tasks.design: Keep attendance, discussion and critical learning with the teacher. Existing reference materials in {DOCS} support reflection; no automated attendance substitute is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professional competence requires engagement with teaching and occupational practice.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change removes the need to participate and evaluate what is learned.
tasks.still_hard: A useful workshop idea may not fit the teacher's students or equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Ask questions, compare practice and decide what is worth applying.
tasks.altitude: Professional learning obligations and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Participation and critical professional learning retain all labour; source discovery belongs to a separate task.

assumptions: Boundary is actual attendance and engagement, excluding course discovery owned by task 6690 and booking administration not stated here.
No structured learning-completion input is newly required by a machine step.
Existing native reference access remains sufficient. No new process or maintenance is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Current development requirements and session formats
research_questions: Which learning can be applied to actual classroom or workshop practice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Attendance and professional reflection remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and schedule lessons with colleagues

steps.what: Confer with staff to plan lessons following approved curricula
Schedule the agreed lessons and confirm shared rooms and equipment

tasks.design: Keep joint lesson planning with staff and use native {CALENDAR} resource views to schedule the agreed sequence. The teacher checks shared room and tool availability before confirming; the scheduler does not choose learning content.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed lesson timing must be compared with staff and workshop resource bookings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native availability and recurring booking templates reduce repeated date entry.
tasks.still_hard: A free room may lack the equipment or preparation time the lesson needs.
tasks.human_edge: Agree educationally sensible sequencing and recognise hidden practical dependencies.
tasks.altitude: Less schedule entry; collaborative lesson decisions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Align lesson schedules with workshop resources

evidence.claim: Native resource calendars can reduce date comparison and repeated entry; this is E1 model knowledge without measured digest evidence.

assumptions: Boundary is teacher collaboration and scheduling for an agreed lesson sequence, excluding lesson-material production and live instruction.

The teacher produces lesson IDs, order, duration, staff, room type, equipment and setup constraints in s1 and retained s2 time. All 70 discussion hours and 15 scheduling hours remain for capture, checks and exceptions.

Staff and resource booking owners supply existing availability through normal calendars; no new colleague capture duty is required. Missing resource details or conflicts return to manual discussion within retained s2 time.
Test native recurring bookings and resource calendars before custom code; additional calendar maintenance is counted below.
unknowns: Coverage and accuracy of resource calendars
research_questions: Can native availability reduce scheduling effort after counting equipment and setup checks?

already_counted.description: Lesson constraints, schedule checks and confirmation

incremental.description: Maintain recurring booking templates and handle calendar faults
Maintain resource calendar access and definitions

approvals.approved_version: Exact lesson sequence, staff, dates, rooms, equipment and setup intervals; changes require renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70+15=85; gross 15%, minus three focal upkeep gives 12% central net. Low assumes five schedule-entry hours removable when resource availability remains incomplete; collaboration stays full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce shared lesson scheduling while retaining extracurricular guidance, programme collaboration and professional learning.
reach: Coordinate reliable workshop calendars with timetable staff
role.ambitious_version: A vocational teacher with fewer repeated schedule entries and unchanged attention to colleagues and students.
